🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Richard Lloyd, the co-founding guitarist of the legendary New York rock band Television, has died at 75.

Lloyd died on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee. His family confirmed his death in a statement shared with The New York Times, saying he died of cholangiocarcinoma, a form of bile duct cancer, with which he was diagnosed in March 2026. "His loving wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays were with him at the end," the family said.

Born in Pittsburgh in 1951, Lloyd helped form Television in New York City in 1973 alongside Tom Verlaine. The band became one of the defining acts of the CBGB punk scene, and its 1977 debut album, Marquee Moon, is widely regarded as one of the greatest rock albums ever made, celebrated for the intertwined guitar work of Lloyd and Verlaine. Television followed it with Adventure in 1978 and a self-titled album in 1992.

Lloyd left Television in 2007 and built a respected solo career, releasing a series of solo albums and playing guitar with Matthew Sweet, among others. In 2018, he published his memoir, Everything Is Combustible: Television, CBGB's and Five Decades of Rock and Roll.

Lloyd revealed his cancer diagnosis publicly in August 2026, when friends launched a fundraiser to help with his medical bills. Patti Smith was among those who donated, saying his musical contribution "inspired us all."

Rest in Peace, Richard Lloyd.

Sources: The New York Times, confirming his death and the family's statement; Rolling Stone; Consequence.
